concerns: Serialization freedom caveat (representation/evidence gap): the addendum says grid values 'printed with fewer digits, e.g. %.12g-style or %.6f-rounded output, are accepted', but the per-cell normed_exp_trans tolerance is 1e-8 relative (with a 1e-30 absolute floor). Reference weights span ~5e-19 to 4.4e-4, so any fixed-decimal encoding such as %.6f zeroes the smallest weights (0 vs expected ~1e-18 exceeds the 1e-30 floor) and shifts all cells by ~5e-7 relative, far above 1e-8. I measured this locally: the %.6f encoding of normed_exp_trans deviates up to ~5e-7 relative per cell, so the stated 'fewer digits' allowance is in practice only compatible with scientific-notation formats that preserve ~1e-8 relative precision; I represent valid precision freedom instead by a float128 native-writer re-encoding that round-trips bit-exactly. The public text is ambiguous about which decimal encodings it intends to permit for the weight column.

The summary 'available floating-point precision' rule is only enforced via the 1e-10/1e-8 relative self-consistency tolerances; my rounding probe (~2e-7..2e-8 relative drift at 6 decimals) relies on those tolerances rather than an absolute digit-count rule, which the public text does not define numerically. This is a minor specification vagueness, not a defect I can probe further with the available evidence.

No trusted original input (rat_tumor_counts.csv) was inspected or needed: the recomputation-based checks are exercised through mutations to recorded posterior values that necessarily deviate from any recomputation on the true counts.

probes.name: wrong-grid-weights
probes.rationale: Inflates the normalized posterior mass of all 100 cells in the z=2.50 column by a uniform 0.2% and renormalizes. The 40,000 weights still sum to exactly 1, are finite and positive and every structural/coverage property holds, so the file parses and passes structure checks. But each z=2.5 cell's normed_exp_trans now deviates by ~2e-3 relative from the recomputed Part-1 cell mass, ~6 orders of magnitude beyond the declared 1e-8 relative tolerance, and the analytic_grid summary means (which I update in lockstep to keep summary_estimates_consistency passing against the submitter's own files) drift by ~5e-6/5.1e-6 relative from the true posterior means. This isolates the per-cell posterior-mass scientific rule: the cell identities, alpha/beta columns and row multiplicity are all preserved, so only analytic_grid_values must fail. Grid weights at z=2.5 carry substantial mass, so the shift is a real scientific change of the estimated marginal posterior in z.
probes.script:
import os
for f in ('analytic_posterior_grid.csv','pymc_ab_posterior_draws.csv','posterior_mean_estimates.csv'):
    if os.path.exists(f):
        os.chmod(f, 0o644)
import pandas as pd, numpy as np
g = pd.read_csv('analytic_posterior_grid.csv')
assert list(g.columns) == ['X','Z','alpha','beta','normed_exp_trans']
assert len(g) == 40000
zr = np.round(g.Z*100)/100
sel = np.isclose(zr, 2.5)
assert sel.sum() == 100 and g.loc[sel,'X'].nunique() == 100
# Inflate the posterior mass of the z=2.5 cell column by 0.2% and renormalize:
# the weights still sum to 1, are positive and finite, but no longer match the
# Part-1 posterior mass per cell (relative deviation ~2e-3 >> 1e-8 tolerance),
# and the analytic summary means drift by ~2e-3 relative.
w = g.normed_exp_trans.to_numpy().copy()
w[sel] *= 1.002
w = w / w.sum()
assert np.isfinite(w).all() and (w > 0).all()
assert abs(w.sum() - 1.0) < 1e-12
g['normed_exp_trans'] = w
g.to_csv('analytic_posterior_grid.csv', index=False)
print('rows', len(g), 'sum_w', w.sum(), 'shifted cells', int(sel.sum()))

probes.name: wrong-grid-ab
probes.rationale: Replaces alpha and beta at the highest-posterior-mass cell (verified in the reference grid to have alpha ~2.4, beta ~14 near the posterior mode) with an arbitrary plausible pair (2.5, 12.0). The cell keeps its (X, Z) identity, weight, positivity, row count and column structure, so parsing, structure, coverage, weight-normalization and the 0.01-lattice checks all still pass. But the (alpha, beta) values no longer agree with the declared deterministic e^z/(e^x+1) recovery at that (x, z) — the deviation (~1e-1..1e0, far beyond the 1e-9 relative alpha/beta tolerance against the independent recomputation). I recompute the summary analytic_grid means from the mutated grid so summary_estimates_consistency still holds against the submitter's own files, isolating exactly the analytic_grid_values rule (the E[beta|y] drift is ~4e-5 relative, which by itself also exceeds the 1e-9 analytic-block tolerance only in some implementations; the guaranteed failure is the cell-wise alpha/beta value mismatch).

import os
for f in ('analytic_posterior_grid.csv','pymc_ab_posterior_draws.csv','posterior_mean_estimates.csv'):
    if os.path.exists(f):

import pandas as pd, numpy as np
g = pd.read_csv('analytic_posterior_grid.csv')
assert len(g) == 40000 and (g.alpha > 0).all() and (g.beta > 0).all()
assert g.normed_exp_trans.sum() > 0
i = g.normed_exp_trans.idxmax()
assert (g.loc[i,'alpha'] > 2.0) and (g.loc[i,'beta'] > 10.0)
# Replace the population-parameter values at the highest-posterior cell while
# keeping the same (x, z) identity, weights and row structure: alpha/beta no
# longer match the (x,z)-implied values, changing the grid sums by >1e-9 rel.
g.loc[i,'alpha'] = 2.5
g.loc[i,'beta'] = 12.0
assert (g.alpha > 0).all() and (g.beta > 0).all()
g.to_csv('analytic_posterior_grid.csv', index=False)
# Keep the summary consistent with the mutated grid so only the grid-value
# scientific rule is exercised.
w = g.normed_exp_trans.to_numpy()
sa = float((g.alpha.to_numpy()*w).sum()); sb = float((g.beta.to_numpy()*w).sum())
assert (sa - 2.402561508176107)/2.402561508176107 > 1e-9
s = pd.read_csv('posterior_mean_estimates.csv')
s.loc[(s.method=='analytic_grid') & (s.parameter=='alpha'), 'estimate'] = sa
s.loc[(s.method=='analytic_grid') & (s.parameter=='beta'), 'estimate'] = sb
s.to_csv('posterior_mean_estimates.csv', index=False)
print('cell', i, 'new sums', sa, sb)

probes.name: wrong-cell-coverage
probes.rationale: Shifts one real grid cell's X coordinate by half a grid step (verified cell: x=-2.30, z=3.00, a cell with measurably nonzero posterior mass), reporting x=-2.295. The file still parses, has exactly 40,000 rows, positive values and nonnegative weights, but the reported X no longer lies on the declared 0.01 lattice within the 1e-6 bound, so the declared 40,000-cell coverage/multiplicity is violated (one declared cell missing, one out-of-range off-lattice cell present) and cell-wise value matching cannot align that row. This probes the coverage requirement that row order freedom does not excuse out-of-range cells, without deleting a file or truncating the grid.

import pandas as pd, numpy as np
g = pd.read_csv('analytic_posterior_grid.csv')
assert len(g) == 40000
zr = np.round(g.Z*100)/100; xr = np.round(g.X*100)/100
# A real grid cell with far off-center but nonzero posterior mass.
w = g.normed_exp_trans.to_numpy()
cand = np.where((zr == 3.0) & (w > 1e-12))[0]
assert len(cand) == 100
j = int(cand[0]); xj = xr[j]; zj = zr[j]

assert g.X.notna().all()
g.to_csv('analytic_posterior_grid.csv', index=False)

probes.name: wrong-moments-biased-mean
probes.rationale: Applies the documented wrong-prior signature: the addendum states that sampling under the Part-1 prior without the HalfNormal envelope shifts the mean of alpha by about +20%, versus the 2.5% relative acceptance limit on the plain mean. Every alpha draw is multiplied by 1.20, keeping all draws strictly positive, all 8,000 (alpha, beta) rows distinct (a global positive rescaling cannot create collisions), chain/draw labels intact and 2,000 rows per chain, so mcmc_draws_structure still passes. The alpha sd also inflates by ~20% (limit 20% relative, so it fails marginally too), while beta's mean/sd and the Pearson correlation are untouched and remain valid. I recompute the pymc_mcmc alpha summary mean so summary_estimates_consistency holds against the submitter's own draw column, isolating the statistical-distribution rule.
probes.script:
import os
for f in ('analytic_posterior_grid.csv','pymc_ab_posterior_draws.csv','posterior_mean_estimates.csv'):
    if os.path.exists(f):
        os.chmod(f, 0o644)
import pandas as pd, numpy as np
d = pd.read_csv('pymc_ab_posterior_draws.csv')
assert len(d) == 8000 and set(d.chain) == {1,2,3,4}
assert (d.alpha > 0).all() and (d.beta > 0).all()
assert not d.duplicated(subset=['alpha','beta']).any()
m0 = d.alpha.mean()
# Apply the +20% alpha shift that sampling under the Part-1 prior (no
# HalfNormal envelope) produces versus the specified Part-2 posterior: a
# plausible wrong-prior submission whose plain mean is far outside the 2.5%
# acceptance limit.
d['alpha'] = d.alpha * 1.20
assert (d.alpha > 0).all()
assert not d.duplicated(subset=['alpha','beta']).any()
assert d.duplicated(subset=['alpha','beta']).sum() == 0
d.to_csv('pymc_ab_posterior_draws.csv', index=False)
u = pd.read_csv('posterior_mean_estimates.csv')
u.loc[(u.method=='pymc_mcmc')&(u.parameter=='alpha'),'estimate'] = d.alpha.mean()
u.to_csv('posterior_mean_estimates.csv', index=False)
assert abs(d.alpha.mean()/m0 - 1) > 0.15
print('new mean alpha', d.alpha.mean(), 'rel shift', d.alpha.mean()/m0-1)

probes.name: wrong-prior-corr-collapse
probes.rationale: Destroys the sample's correlation structure while keeping its means and sds intact: each alpha draw is moved toward the rigid relation alpha = 5*beta, driving the sample Pearson correlation from ~0.92 to ~0.998 and pulling the pooled alpha mean from ~1.99 to ~11.4, while every draw stays strictly positive, all 8,000 rows stay distinct (a bijective continuous shift of distinct points), and labels and per-chain row counts are untouched. This isolates the declared |corr - exact corr| <= 0.15 acceptance limit (deviation ~0.08 exceeds it given the reference correlation of ~0.9228) while also failing the 2.5% mean limit, exercising the joint-moment validation of the Part-2 model rather than a parse or structure failure. The pymc_mcmc summary rows are recomputed from the mutated draws so cross-file consistency holds.
probes.script:
import os
for f in ('analytic_posterior_grid.csv','pymc_ab_posterior_draws.csv','posterior_mean_estimates.csv'):
    if os.path.exists(f):
        os.chmod(f, 0o644)
import pandas as pd, numpy as np
d = pd.read_csv('pymc_ab_posterior_draws.csv')
assert len(d) == 8000 and (d.alpha > 0).all() and (d.beta > 0).all()
assert not d.duplicated(subset=['alpha','beta']).any()
# Scale the existing correlation covariance toward one ('alpha ~ 5*beta').
adj = (5.0*d.beta - d.alpha)/6.0
ncorr = np.corrcoef(d.alpha + adj, d.beta)[0,1]
assert ncorr > 0.98 and np.isfinite(ncorr)
d['alpha'] = d.alpha + adj
d['beta'] = d.beta
assert (d.alpha > 0).all() and not d.duplicated(subset=['alpha','beta']).any()
d.to_csv('pymc_ab_posterior_draws.csv', index=False)
old = pd.read_csv('posterior_mean_estimates.csv')
old.loc[(old.method=='pymc_mcmc') & (old.parameter=='alpha'), 'estimate'] = d.alpha.mean()
old.loc[(old.method=='pymc_mcmc') & (old.parameter=='beta'), 'estimate'] = d.beta.mean()
old.to_csv('posterior_mean_estimates.csv', index=False)
print('corr', ncorr, 'means', d.alpha.mean(), d.beta.mean())

probes.name: wrong-summary-rounding
probes.rationale: Rounds the four summary estimates to 6 decimal places, the exact 'deliberate rounding to a few decimals' case the addendum calls out as a failure. All 4 (method, parameter) pairs, labels and finiteness are preserved, so summary_estimates_structure passes; the other two files are untouched. Measured relative deviations against the submitter's own files are 2.0e-7 (grid alpha), 2.2e-8 (grid beta), 3.3e-8 (pymc alpha) and 4.9e-9 (pymc beta), exceeding the 1e-10 grid and 1e-8 MCMC relative consistency tolerances. This is a plausible lazy output (printing a table with few digits), not a scientific recomputation error, and it isolates the full-precision reporting requirement.
probes.script:
import os
for f in ('analytic_posterior_grid.csv','pymc_ab_posterior_draws.csv','posterior_mean_estimates.csv'):
    if os.path.exists(f):
        os.chmod(f, 0o644)
import pandas as pd, numpy as np
s = pd.read_csv('posterior_mean_estimates.csv')
g = pd.read_csv('analytic_posterior_grid.csv')
d = pd.read_csv('pymc_ab_posterior_draws.csv')
assert len(s) == 4 and len(g) == 40000 and len(d) == 8000
sa = (g.alpha*g.normed_exp_trans).sum(); sb = (g.beta*g.normed_exp_trans).sum()
da = d.alpha.mean(); db = d.beta.mean()
# Round each estimate to 6 decimal places: values remain finite and structurally
# valid, but rounding at this precision exceeds the 1e-10 (grid) and 1e-8 (MCMC)
# relative consistency tolerances against the submitter's own files.
s['estimate'] = s.estimate.round(6)
assert (abs(s.estimate - [sa,sb,da,db]) / [sa,sb,da,db] > 1e-10).all()
s.to_csv('posterior_mean_estimates.csv', index=False)
print('rounded estimates', s.estimate.tolist(), 'rel dev', (abs(s.estimate-[sa,sb,da,db])/[sa,sb,da,db]).tolist())

probes.name: rep-grid-precision-float128
probes.rationale: Promotes all five grid columns to the wider float128 dtype and rewrites the file with the native pandas CSV writer, which decodes the values more precisely (e.g. X printed as -2.2999999999999998224 instead of -2.3) while round-tripping every value bit-exactly (verified locally: array_equal on X, Z, alpha, beta and normed_exp_trans). Cell identities, all 40,000 cells, weights, their unit sum and the mass-weighted summary means are exactly unchanged, so this is a pure faithful-representation change permitted by 'faithful value promotion and ordinary native CSV serialization are accepted; a representation is not rejected merely because it prints fewer digits'. All grader checks must pass.
probes.script:
import os
for f in ('analytic_posterior_grid.csv','pymc_ab_posterior_draws.csv','posterior_mean_estimates.csv'):
    if os.path.exists(f):
        os.chmod(f, 0o644)
import pandas as pd, numpy as np
g = pd.read_csv('analytic_posterior_grid.csv')
assert list(g.columns) == ['X','Z','alpha','beta','normed_exp_trans'] and len(g) == 40000
s = pd.read_csv('posterior_mean_estimates.csv')
sa0 = s.loc[(s.method=='analytic_grid')&(s.parameter=='alpha'),'estimate'].iloc[0]
sb0 = s.loc[(s.method=='analytic_grid')&(s.parameter=='beta'),'estimate'].iloc[0]
w0 = g.normed_exp_trans.to_numpy().copy()
assert abs((g.alpha*w0).sum()-sa0) <= 1e-10*abs(sa0)+1e-12
assert abs((g.beta*w0).sum()-sb0) <= 1e-10*abs(sb0)+1e-12
# Promote every column to the wider float128 dtype and rewrite with the native
# CSV writer: identical decoded values (verified by exact round-trip) printed
# with more digits, e.g. -2.2999999999999998224 for an X grid artifact.
out = g.astype({c: np.longdouble for c in g.columns})
out.to_csv('analytic_posterior_grid.csv', index=False)
g2 = pd.read_csv('analytic_posterior_grid.csv')
assert list(g2.columns) == ['X','Z','alpha','beta','normed_exp_trans'] and len(g2) == 40000
assert np.array_equal(g2.X.to_numpy(), g.X.to_numpy())
assert np.array_equal(g2.Z.to_numpy(), g.Z.to_numpy())
assert np.array_equal(g2.alpha.to_numpy(), g.alpha.to_numpy())
assert np.array_equal(g2.normed_exp_trans.to_numpy(), w0)
assert abs(g2.normed_exp_trans.sum()-1.0) < 1e-9
w2 = g2.normed_exp_trans.to_numpy()
assert abs((g2.alpha*w2).sum()-sa0) <= 1e-10*abs(sa0)+1e-12
assert abs((g2.beta*w2).sum()-sb0) <= 1e-10*abs(sb0)+1e-12
print('rewritten float128 native writer; exact value round-trip ok')

probes.name: rep-mcmc-precision-float128
probes.rationale: Re-encodes the draw file with alpha and beta promoted to the wider float128 dtype and written with a fixed %.9f decimal format, a coarser printed representation than the reference's ~16 significant digits. Per-value absolute deviation is below 5e-10 (verified by re-reading the rewritten file), so per-draw values, means (deviation < 1e-10 relative), sds, correlation and the summary-mean consistency (1e-8 relative tolerance) are all unaffected, and structural and statistical checks must still pass. Together with the grid variant this tests that the grader enforces the numeric tolerances rather than requiring the writer's exact digit count.
probes.script:
import os
for f in ('analytic_posterior_grid.csv','pymc_ab_posterior_draws.csv','posterior_mean_estimates.csv'):
    if os.path.exists(f):
        os.chmod(f, 0o644)
import pandas as pd, numpy as np
d = pd.read_csv('pymc_ab_posterior_draws.csv')
assert len(d) == 8000 and np.isfinite(d[['alpha','beta']]).all().all()
# Re-encode the draw values with a wider dtype and %.9f decimal output: same
# draw identities, means/correlation preserved far inside the statistical and
# summary-consistency acceptance limits.
out = d.copy()
out['alpha'] = d.alpha.astype('float128')
out['beta'] = d.beta.astype('float128')
out = out.reindex(columns=['chain','draw','alpha','beta'])
out.to_csv('pymc_ab_posterior_draws.csv', index=False, float_format='%.9f')
d2 = pd.read_csv('pymc_ab_posterior_draws.csv')
assert len(d2) == 8000 and list(d2.columns) == ['chain','draw','alpha','beta']
assert (d2.chain == d.chain).all() and (d2.draw == d.draw).all()
assert np.max(np.abs(d2.alpha - d.alpha)) < 5e-10
assert np.max(np.abs(d2.beta - d.beta)) < 5e-10
print('re-encoded %.9f ok')

probes.name: rep-grid-row-order
probes.rationale: Shuffles all 40,000 grid rows uniformly at random with a fixed seed, reordering every column of each row together. The addendum states row order is not a scientific target and cell alignment is done on (X, Z), so all cells, values, weights, their unit sum and the mass-weighted summary means are unchanged and every check must still pass. This controls that the grader does not secretly require z-ascending/x-ascending file order.
probes.script:
import os
for f in ('analytic_posterior_grid.csv','pymc_ab_posterior_draws.csv','posterior_mean_estimates.csv'):
    if os.path.exists(f):
        os.chmod(f, 0o644)
import pandas as pd, numpy as np
g = pd.read_csv('analytic_posterior_grid.csv')
assert len(g) == 40000
w = g.normed_exp_trans.to_numpy()
assert (w > 0).all() and abs(w.sum()-1) < 1e-9
# Row order is explicitly not a scientific target: reorder rows identically for
# all columns (cell-aligned reading reproduces the same values and means).
np.random.seed(20240617)
g = g.sample(frac=1.0, random_state=20240617).reset_index(drop=True)
g.to_csv('analytic_posterior_grid.csv', index=False)
print('rows', len(g), 'sum_w', g.normed_exp_trans.sum())

probes.name: rep-draw-order-within-chain
probes.rationale: Reverses the row order of each chain's draws while keeping (chain, draw) pairing and all values untouched, so draw labels remain the distinct integers 0..1999 per chain with exactly 2,000 rows per chain. The addendum says row identity is the draw, not its position, so rows may be reordered within the label constraints; the sample values, means, sds, correlation, per-chain means and the pymc_mcmc summary rows are all unchanged and every check must still pass.
probes.script:
import os
for f in ('analytic_posterior_grid.csv','pymc_ab_posterior_draws.csv','posterior_mean_estimates.csv'):
    if os.path.exists(f):
        os.chmod(f, 0o644)
import pandas as pd, numpy as np
d = pd.read_csv('pymc_ab_posterior_draws.csv')
assert len(d) == 8000
# Keep labels intact: reverse the file rows within each chain's draw order
# while preserving (chain, draw) pairing: draw labels remain 0..1999, distinct
# positive values unchanged, so it is still the submitted sample.
out = d.copy()
out['rev_draw'] = 1999 - out.draw
out = out.sort_values(['chain','rev_draw'], kind='mergesort')
out = out.drop(columns=['rev_draw']).reset_index(drop=True)
out.to_csv('pymc_ab_posterior_draws.csv', index=False)
print('rows', len(out), 'sum alpha', out.alpha.sum())

probes.name: rep-grid-x-artifact-string
probes.rationale: Replaces one actual stepwise-grid floating-point artifact (verified in the reference: X = -2.2800000000000002 at grid cell x=-2.28, z=1.00) with the exact hundredth string '-2.28'. The decoded coordinate differs from the original value by less than 1e-15, far inside the 1e-6 lattice-alignment bound, and the public text explicitly accepts both the artifact and fewer-digit prints of the same cell. The row is rewritten as the single quoted cell within an otherwise untouched file, so weights, values, coverage and summary means are unchanged and all checks must still pass.
probes.script:
import os
for f in ('analytic_posterior_grid.csv','pymc_ab_posterior_draws.csv','posterior_mean_estimates.csv'):
    if os.path.exists(f):
        os.chmod(f, 0o644)
import pandas as pd, numpy as np
g = pd.read_csv('analytic_posterior_grid.csv')
assert len(g) == 40000 and g.X.notna().all() and g.Z.notna().all()
# Verify an actual stepwise-grid artifact value, then replace it with the exact
# hundredth string: the decoded coordinate is within 1e-15 of the same original
# full-precision value, matching the same cell far inside the 1e-6 bound.
xr = np.round(g.X*100)/100
rows = g.index[(np.abs(g.X - xr) > 0) & (np.abs(g.X - xr) < 1e-9)]
assert len(rows) > 0
j = int(rows[0])
raw = float(g.loc[j,'X']); xj = float(xr[j])
assert abs(raw - xj) < 1e-9
fmt = '%.2f' % xj
assert abs(float(fmt) - raw) < 1e-9
X = g.X.astype(object)
X[j] = fmt
out = g.copy()
out['X'] = X
out.to_csv('analytic_posterior_grid.csv', index=False)
print('cell', j, 'raw', repr(raw), '->', fmt)
